subject: science
passage: In the 1940s, working with corn plants at Cold Spring Harbor on Long Island, New York, the geneticist Barbara McClintock noticed that some kernels bore streaks and spots of color that the genetics of the day could not easily explain. Puzzled by the way these patterns appeared and disappeared across generations of her own carefully controlled crosses, ______ When she presented the idea in 1951, many colleagues found it baffling, and decades passed before similar "jumping genes" were found in other organisms; in 1983, she received an unshared Nobel Prize.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: McClintock's conclusion was that certain genetic elements could move from one position on a chromosome to another, switching nearby genes on and off.
choices.B: McClintock concluded that certain genetic elements could move from one position on a chromosome to another, switching nearby genes on and off.
choices.C: certain genetic elements, McClintock concluded, could move from one position on a chromosome to another, switching nearby genes on and off.
choices.D: the conclusion McClintock reached was that certain genetic elements could move from one position on a chromosome to another, switching nearby genes on and off.

explanation.why: The introductory phrase "Puzzled by the way these patterns appeared and disappeared" describes a person: the scientist who was puzzled. A modifier at the start of a sentence applies to the subject that comes right after the comma, so that subject must be McClintock herself.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The subject is "conclusion"; "McClintock's" only describes it, so the sentence says the conclusion was puzzled.
explanation.B: Correct. "McClintock" comes right after the introductory phrase, so it is clear that she was the one who was puzzled.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The subject is "certain genetic elements"; "McClintock concluded" is only an interrupting phrase, so the sentence says the genetic elements were puzzled.
explanation.D: Incorrect. This makes "the conclusion" the subject, so the sentence says the conclusion was puzzled.
